trajectory_summary: The call opens cold with a legitimacy check and an apparent roof-replacement objection, but the rep converts that objection into a dual-service (roof + solar) opportunity within seconds and rides it to a booked appointment. The rep holds setter scope on technical roofing/efficiency questions by deferring to the specialist, and proactively solicits handoff content at the close. Energy in the call builds steadily from suspicion to a customer-initiated scheduling offer.
outcome_dispute: v1 tag is unknown/unclear; observed trajectory clearly supports a booked appointment with day and time locked (Thursday the 30th, 9:30 AM), so if v1 tagged this as anything other than booked, that should be corrected.

observed_outcome.quote: Awesome. So we'll plan on Thursday, which is the thirtieth, 09:30AM.
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day and time were locked and the rep frames it as the specialist 'bringing it by,' indicating an in-person appointment; no spouse or co-owner was mentioned anywhere in the call.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: This call is framed around an existing solar design and a new roofing cross-sell rather than fresh bill collection; no utility bill amount or usage figure is mentioned anywhere in the transcript, consistent with this being a repeat-touch/recycled lead where bill data may already be on file.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never explicitly asks what interested the customer in solar; the call instead centers on rescheduling a design review and the newly surfaced roof-replacement need, likely because prior interest was already captured on an earlier touch that this call is following up on.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: specific recap and handoff detail capture
primary_coaching_focus.quote: kinda what we're looking into, and we'll take it from there.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The rep did the hard part well -- she asked what to pass along and gathered two concrete, usable details (missing shingles/insurance question, roof efficiency question) -- but then summarized the handoff generically instead of naming those details back, which risks losing them before the specialist call.

key_moments.quote: Yeah. So I'm here with Ion Solar. I was reaching out because we built a solar design for the home, and we were supposed to go through it with you last week but never had the chance.
key_moments.stewart_read: The primary read here is that this is a recycled/repeat-touch lead -- the rep references a prior solar design and a missed appointment 'last week,' which strongly indicates an existing Ion relationship rather than a cold first contact. The intro is thin on state/referral framing, but the follow-up-call context largely explains why a fuller legitimacy anchor wasn't rebuilt from scratch.

key_moments.quote: The reason I ask is because here at Ion, we actually do the roof and the solar. So I'm more than happy to put together a a roof option as well just so you can see what that looks like,
key_moments.stewart_read: This is actually a positive execution of the cross-sell bridge, not a miss -- the rep hears 'replacement' and immediately routes to Ion's in-house roofing offer within seconds, closely matching the schema's positive exemplar pattern.

key_moments.quote: And is it just regular asphalt shingles?
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep and customer both struggle to identify the roof material (customer offers only 'brownish color'), and rep guesses at categories (wood, concrete) rather than working from a defined list, showing some unpreparedness on roofing verification specifics now that roofing is part of the pitch.

key_moments.quote: I don't think so. No. K. Gotcha. See if you guys can help with that because there are some shingles missing in my roof.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer volunteers a concrete roof-damage detail (missing shingles) and asks Ion directly to help with insurance, an unprompted signal of real roofing need and investment in the outcome, which strengthens the combined roof+solar opportunity for the closer.
